name: Commodore 64
description: Commodore's 8-bit home computer, released in 1982, named for its 64 KB of RAM. Its sprites, smooth scrolling and SID sound chip made it a strong games machine, and its price made it the best-selling single computer model. It stayed in production until 1994.
curiosities: Guinness World Records lists it as the best-selling single computer model.
SID designer Bob Yannes later co-founded the synthesizer maker Ensoniq.
Its 1541 disk drive has its own 6502 processor and can run code independently of the computer.
